newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Fifteen hurt as police disperse opposition rally.
newsitem.headline: Fifteen hurt as police disperse opposition rally.

text.p: At least 15 people were injured when police fired teargas and used batons to disperse a rally by the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in northeastern Sylhet town, witnesses said.
They said BNP organised the rally to wrap up a day-long local strike to protest against poor communications and soaring food prices.
"The strike passed off peacefully. But violence erupted after some activists pelted stones at police guarding the rally," one witness said.
"Police responded by firing teargas and making random use of batons. At least 15 people were injured," he told Reuters.
Police said they acted in self defence. It was not immediately known if police arrested anyone.

The strike, called by the BNP headed by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, paralysed transport in Sylhet and neighbouring areas. "Buses, trains and other transport were all shut, but airline flights operated normally," one journalist in Sylhet said.
Officials in Sylhet, headquarters of the country's largest tea growing region, could face another stoppage this week as the BNP had vowed tougher protest against police action.
The BNP said it would announce further actions later on Tuesday.
